claim_text: Expedia confirmed that attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider
summary: Skift reports that Expedia Group confirmed on Thursday Nov 12 that attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider, in a supply chain attack that also hit multiple other companies.
detail: Expedia gave the same wording to Skift and, on Nov 18, to The Seattle Times, which quotes it in full. We found no Expedia newsroom page with it. Expedia did not name the vendor.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Expedia's own statement to two independent outlets (Skift and The Seattle Times); no company page exists to cite.

claim_text: Expedia says it contained the issue, is investigating with outside experts, and that its platforms remain safe
summary: Skift's summary says Expedia contained the issue when it became aware and is investigating with outside experts. The Seattle Times quotes Expedia that it is actively investigating and its platforms remain safe to use.
detail: The containment and outside-experts points come from Skift's summary text. It is the company's own claim and cannot be checked from outside.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Company's own claim, as summarised by one outlet.

claim_text: A group called n0n claims it stole Expedia data and threatened to publish it unless the company settled
summary: Skift says n0n threatened to publish data it says is Expedia's unless the company settled, per Cybernews, with no ransom amount shown. Cybernews first reported the listing in an article dated Oct 9.
detail: Skift says Expedia's confirmation came after several security sites reported the group's claims that week. Cyber Daily, a second outlet, says the group's leak post claiming more than one terabyte of Expedia data was dated Nov 3, after Cybernews's Oct 9 report, and that Expedia declined to comment to it before its Nov 12 statement. We did not look at the group's page. The claim comes only through press.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cybernews and Cyber Daily, two independent outlets, report the group's claim and Skift relays it; the group's own post is not cited.

claim_text: n0n claims it stole about one billion Expedia records
summary: Cybernews says the group claims more than 830 million loyalty program rows, 58 million traveler profiles and over 333 million account records with emails and password-like tokens, among other files.
detail: These are the group's own figures. Cybernews first reported them in an article dated Oct 9, and Cyber Daily quotes the same loyalty-row figure from the group's Nov 3 post, along with its claim of more than one terabyte. Rows are not people: one traveler can appear in many rows and tables, so the figures do not say how many travelers are affected. Nobody has shown the size. Cybernews checked only the roughly 500MB posted. Skift says the scale is unconfirmed, and Expedia told The Seattle Times the claims are unverified and it cannot confirm them.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: Two outlets (Cybernews, s002 and s007, and Cyber Daily, s008) relay the group's own claim, but nobody has checked it; Expedia calls the claims unverified and says it cannot confirm them.

claim_text: Expedia calls the group's claims 'unverified claims from criminals' and says it cannot confirm their accuracy
summary: Expedia told The Seattle Times on Nov 18 that the figures are unverified claims from criminals and that it cannot confirm their accuracy. It also said it takes travelers' privacy extremely seriously.
detail: This is a company statement through one outlet. It does not say the data is fake; it says Expedia cannot confirm it. It does not say whether customer data was taken.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Company's own words, quoted by one outlet.

claim_text: The group posted over 500MB of files, and Cybernews says they hold Expedia customer records such as emails, booking events and loyalty details
summary: Cybernews researchers say over 500MB of posted CSV files hold, among other things, about 150,000 old account records with emails and bcrypt hashes, about 400,000 loyalty records, 120,000 traveler profiles and 100,000 booking events.
detail: These are Cybernews's descriptions of the files. Cyber Daily separately says the posted archive appears to be an extract, with 11 folders listing hundreds of thousands of email addresses linked to travel data such as log-ins, hotel stays and loyalty points, and that the data may be old given the date ranges in some files. It says some of the emails appear in earlier breaches and many do not. Expedia has not confirmed the files are genuine. Cybernews wrote on Nov 17 that it had not heard back from Expedia. Bcrypt hashes make cracking harder but not impossible, and Cybernews warns old accounts could be targeted.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets' descriptions of the posted files; neither can show the files came from Expedia, and the company has not confirmed them.

claim_text: Whether Expedia customer data was taken
summary: Expedia's statement as reported does not say what information was exposed. Skift says the data exposed and the scale are unconfirmed.
detail: The only evidence of customer data being taken is the group's posted files as described by Cybernews (c005). Expedia has not said whether those files are genuine or whether any customer was affected.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Expedia's statement is silent on data; Cybernews says it got no confirmation.

claim_text: Which vendor it was and how the attacker got in
summary: Expedia did not identify the compromised vendor, and no source we read gives the method.
detail: Skift says Expedia did not name the vendor. Wiz and Sentra, the researchers who documented the Qubole attack, have not named Expedia among its victims, and BleepingComputer says Qubole had not answered its questions as of Nov 20.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of these sources names Expedia's vendor or the method used against Expedia.

claim_text: Skift reports researchers documented a separate October attack through Qubole, a one-time Expedia vendor, but Expedia has not tied it to this breach
summary: Wiz and Sentra say in their own Nov 9 reports that an attacker used Qubole's AWS credentials from Oct 14 to 26 to take data from customers' cloud accounts; Sentra says dozens were hit. Skift calls Qubole a onetime Expedia vendor.
detail: Sentra says the roles the attacker used were often left in place long after companies stopped using Qubole. Neither Wiz nor Sentra names any victim. Skift says Expedia did not confirm whether its breach is related to Qubole. This is context only: the link to Expedia is not established.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The researchers' own reports describe the Qubole attack; Skift supplies the past Expedia tie and says Expedia has not linked the two.

claim_text: The same supply chain attack hit other companies
summary: Skift reports that Expedia described the attack as one that also affected multiple companies. No company is named in what we read.
detail: See the separate Samsung Ads report on this site. Since Nov 20, BleepingComputer reports that JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard each confirmed an incident at a third-party provider after the same group listed them (c012). None of them has been tied to Expedia's vendor.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Relayed from Expedia's statement by one outlet; the other companies are not named.

claim_text: The group n0n claims it carried out the Qubole attack
summary: Wiz added a note on Nov 11 that a group calling itself n0n had claimed the Qubole intrusion, citing a security newsletter, and BleepingComputer reports the claim was made on Nov 11. This is the same group that claims the Expedia data.
detail: Wiz says it has not tied the campaign to other public activity. The group's claim has not been confirmed, and it does not show that Expedia's vendor was Qubole. We did not look at the group's page.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets relay the group's own claim; nobody has confirmed it.

claim_text: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard each said a third-party provider had an incident after n0n listed them
summary: BleepingComputer reports on Nov 20 that Chase said vendors were hit and some customer names and emails may have been accessed, Visa said a provider in Asia Pacific was involved, and Mastercard said a provider exposed some email addresses.
detail: None of the three named the provider. BleepingComputer says Qubole is suspected but not confirmed. No source links these incidents to Expedia's vendor. Chase's statement was posted on social media and is cited here through BleepingComputer.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet carrying the three companies' statements.
